title: Product & Technical Lead: Learning Analytics & Student Support
summary: Leading multidisciplinary teams of developers, business analysts, and service-area experts to transform the university's Salesforce platform and student support services. Responsible for product strategy, product design, technical architecture, and implementation across MyPlymouth, integrated enquiry services, and responsible learning analytics. My work also includes shaping business cases, phased delivery plans, and service operating models, connecting student needs with implementation priorities and operational delivery.

projects.title: MyPlymouth Platform for Students & Staff
projects.body:
Led the product strategy, design, architecture, and end-to-end implementation of MyPlymouth: a comprehensive redesign and rebrand of the university's Salesforce platform. MyPlymouth brings legacy capabilities into a clearer, modern platform with dedicated experiences for students, academics, professional services, and support staff. Student enquiry tracking, staff referrals, the knowledge base, and a student-facing chatbot are fully rolled out. Engagement insights are also fully rolled out, with the same insights available to students about their own engagement and to staff supporting those students. The platform is fully rolled out to students, professional services, and support staff, with rollout to academics currently underway.

Usage statistics — to be added: student users: TBA; staff users: TBA.
projects.summary: A modern Salesforce platform connecting student support, enquiry management and engagement insights for students and staff.

projects.title: Learning Analytics for Early Intervention
projects.body: Led the strategy, product design, architecture, implementation, and operating-model development of a learning analytics service designed to identify students who may benefit from additional support early in their university journey. The platform brings together defined engagement indicators, including use of digital services, lecture attendance, enrolment completion, and the frequency of other early university touchpoints. It prioritises students who may merit attention, enabling trained student ambassadors to make supportive contact, understand their circumstances, and direct them towards relevant services and resources. Trained student ambassadors deliver the outreach using the system and support process I developed with the team. The service supports structured follow-up when initial engagement concerns appear unresolved and established Plymouth University's first student ambassador outreach service of its kind. A comprehensive operating policy defines which data may be used, how it is handled, and the legitimate support purposes for which it can be applied. Selected insights are surfaced through MyPlymouth, while the learning analytics service remains a distinct product and workstream.
projects.award: Vice-Chancellor's Award for Supporting a Great Student Experience — Highly Commended
projects.summary: Responsible learning analytics enabling timely outreach by student ambassadors.

projects.title: Integrated Student Enquiry & Support Service
projects.body: Led the design and implementation of a new institution-wide student enquiry and support service within MyPlymouth. The service replaced fragmented processes based on email, spreadsheets, and independently operated team systems. All internal student-facing teams have adopted the service, including faculty offices, careers, the Student Hub, disability services, and wellbeing teams. Staff manage and refer enquiries between teams, giving authorised staff a more complete view of each student's support journey. Students can view and track their enquiries, see which team is responsible, follow transfers between services, and know when an enquiry has been resolved. Self-service enquiry creation is not yet available to students. The service also supports referrals and longer-term support or wellbeing interventions. The work also included redesigning how front-line teams collaborate and operate. Consistent service data now makes it possible to identify recurring issues and support ongoing service improvement.
projects.summary: Integrated enquiry management and support for students and staff.

title: Digital Education Product Manager
summary: Building a first class student success platform for the Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry. Member of multiple faculty committees.

projects.title: PULSE Student Success Platform
projects.body:
Led the design, technical architecture, and delivery of PULSE, a new integrated Salesforce platform covering student assessment across the university's medical and dental programmes. Built alongside a team of developers, the platform brings together on-clinic assessment and feedback, dental clinical experience, clinical logging, academic benchmarking, and knowledge testing with longitudinal analysis for students. Robust offline support enables on-clinic assessment and feedback, while analysis tools help students and staff review work and progress. The platform serves students, academics, and administrators. Its capabilities were developed progressively and the features described here were operational by 2023. PULSE remains the primary assessment system across all medical and dental programmes. Several related portfolio entries describe individual capabilities within this platform.

Student usage statistics — to be added: TBA.
projects.summary: An integrated Salesforce assessment platform for medical and dental education.

projects.title: Content Adaptive Progress Testing
projects.body:
A separate development built on PULSE after the initial platform, developed during 2023–2024 and subsequently brought into use. Working alongside academics who led the adaptive-testing concept, I contributed to the associated research and led the design, technical architecture, and implementation of the student results, knowledge analysis, and personalised learning feedback within PULSE. The assessment delivery and question-selection mechanisms were developed separately by others. The approach maps knowledge-test questions to the newly released GMC Medical Licensing Assessment (MLA) content map. Subsequent tests select questions covering topics a student has yet to encounter and topics they have previously answered incorrectly. Students therefore follow different assessment paths through the programme, with the aim of giving each student opportunities to cover all topics and demonstrate correct answers before the final MLA examination. Personalised topic mapping and longitudinal feedback show students their coverage and performance, helping them plan their learning. These feedback capabilities also support standard knowledge testing independently of adaptive question selection.

Research paper reference — to be added: TBA.

projects.summary: Adaptive knowledge testing with personalised MLA topic mapping and longitudinal feedback.

projects.title: On-Clinic Dental Experience Assessment
projects.body: Digitised the assessment of clinical dental experience, replacing paper logs and enabling real-time progression tracking via a specialised mobile-friendly tool for recording and validating clinical experience in dental clinics. Providing process assurance for patient safety and enabling students to work towards their longitudinal GDC requirements. Also enabled capacity management to ensure patient availability for student needs and scheduling. Used across clinical sites across the south-west of England in collaboration with PDSE and Peninsula Dental School, which was ranked first in the UK for dentistry in the Guardian University Guide 2022 while the project was in operation.

projects.title: Personalised Knowledge-Test Feedback
projects.body: Led the design, technical architecture, and implementation of student results analysis and personalised learning feedback within PULSE. Personalised feedback formed part of standard knowledge testing, providing graphical analysis, individual assessment blueprinting, and comparisons with the wider cohort. The later content-adaptive progress testing project extended this feedback with mapping to the newly released GMC Medical Licensing Assessment (MLA) content map. Students can see which topics they have encountered across their programme's knowledge tests, which they have yet to encounter, and where they have answered questions correctly or incorrectly. Topic coverage and performance differ between students, allowing each student to track their own progress and plan their learning. These feedback tools are also available for standard knowledge testing, independently of adaptive question selection.
projects.role: Design & Technical Lead — Student Analysis & Feedback
projects.summary: Personalised topic coverage and performance feedback across medical knowledge tests.

extraProjects.title: Dynamic Assessments
extraProjects.body: A flexible assessment system within PULSE that academic and assessment teams can configure for a wide range of uses. Teams can create and modify assessments, update them, and roll them forward between academic years. Configurable structures support multiple submissions from different users contributing to a single assessment outcome, as well as multiple assessment types completed at one point contributing to different outcomes. Robust validation checks submissions for correctness and validity.
extraProjects.summary: Flexible assessment configuration for academic and assessment teams.

extraProjects.title: Academic Benchmarking
extraProjects.body: A benchmarking tool within PULSE that enables groups of academics or professionals to independently review and mark anonymised benchmark work remotely. Submissions are automatically aggregated and compared, allowing participants to see how their marking relates to that of others without identifying individual markers. The comparisons support discussion and analysis to promote high-quality, consistent assessment standards.
extraProjects.summary: Anonymous comparison of independent marking to support consistent assessment standards.
